scenes.name: Rush, Queensrÿche y el metal progresivo
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Grupos muy apreciados por la subcultura por sus letras elocuentes y cargadas de sentido, una excepción en un género que no privilegia las palabras. El trío canadiense Rush, con letras del batería Neil Peart, es el ejemplo: Weinstein pasó una noche de 1982 en el aparcamiento de un estadio explicando a sus fans la historia de 2112, una teocracia que aplasta a quien quiere hacer su propia música; muchos se sabían las letras de memoria, pero más del 70 % creía que Rush estaba del lado de los sacerdotes. Geoff Tate, de Queensrÿche, es uno de los cantantes más alabados.

podcast.title: Signed Baseball Collector
podcast.body: Getty Lee of Rush was deeply passionate about collecting signed baseballs, with a particular focus on those from the old Negro League. "Getty Lee of Rush used to be very, very big into sign baseballs, especially those from the old Negro League."

xref.title: Joining Rush
xref.body: Neil Peart formally became a member of Rush on July 29th, 1974, a date which coincided with Geddy Lee's 21st birthday. He secured the position after auditioning, replacing founding drummer John Rutsey. His first gig with the band was shortly after, on August 14th, 1974, in Pittsburgh, where Rush opened for Uriah Heep and Manfred Mann. "He got the job and formally became a member of Rush on July 29th, 1974, which just happened to be Gettie Lee's 21st birthday."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Les Claypool Comparison
xref.body: Flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers was used as a point of comparison for Les Claypool's bass playing style, crossed with Geddy Lee of Rush. "If you want to compare Les to anyone, do it with Getty Lee of Rush, crossed with flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Les Claypool's Bass-Driven Style
xref.body: Primus's music, a mix of alternative metal and funk metal, is primarily built around the distinctive bass grooves of singer and bass player Les Claypool. Claypool is described as an inventive player, unafraid to push boundaries, with a style comparable to Geddy Lee of Rush crossed with Flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "Primus, experiments with a mix of alternative metal and funk metal, all built around singer and bass player Les Claypool's grooves. Great player, very inventive, never afraid to push boundaries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personality and Public Persona
xref.body: Despite his powerful and loud drumming style, Neil Peart was known as the "quiet one" within Rush, often described as an introvert and a "reluctant drumming institution." He maintained a very private life, with interviews being rare, and fan meet-and-greets typically handled by Alex Lifeson and Geddy Lee. He was highly articulate, extremely well-read, a deep thinker, and possessed a wicked sense of humor, earning unending respect for his abilities as a drummer, lyricist, and writer. "For someone who played so loud and so hard, Neil was the quiet one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rush Audition and Unique Appearance
xref.body: In 1974, Neil Peart auditioned for Rush as one of five drummers, replacing founding member John Rutsey who was leaving due to health issues and a musical mismatch. At the audition, Alex Lifeson and Geddy Lee initially found Neil's appearance "goofy" because he had short hair during a time when long hair was fashionable. He also brought an unusual Slingerland double bass drum kit, notable for its unusually small bass drums. "Alex and Gettie thought Neil looked goofy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tim Commerford's Background and Influences
xref.body: Tim Commerford, known by various names including Tim Bob and Tim C, grew up in Irvine, south of Los Angeles. His mother was a mathematician and his father an aeronautical engineer who worked on the space shuttle. He and Zack de la Rocha formed their first band, Juvenile Expression, in grade seven, after Zack taught Tim to play bass using the Sex Pistols' "Never Mind the Bollocks" album. Tim also spent hours learning Geddy Lee's bass parts from Rush albums. "Mom was a mathematician while his dad was an aeronautical engineer who actually worked on the space shuttle."
